answer: Ephemeral work auction.** Each identity must win a paid task before it can act, and payment clears only after a fixed horizon of verified output. Clones earn nothing until that window passes, so an attacker finances every fake identity through the full delay. During settlement, a random tide of audit slots flags a fraction of new identities, splitting rewards across a wide velvet of unproven peers and diluting each clone's expected payout below its registration and audit cost.
